B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No separate MCP fee or MCP-specific price was found. Vendor docs require a Coupler.io account and configured data flow; public pricing does not specify whether hosted MCP access is included in a particular plan.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Official pricing page lists Free ($0), Starter ($24/month billed annually or $32/month), Active ($99/month billed annually or $132/month), Pro ($199/month billed annually or $259/month), and Custom (flexible pricing).
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Plan pricing is subscription-based; plans differ by account, destination, refresh, and row limits. Free pricing page lists one account, one user, one source, one destination, and manual refresh. No MCP per-call charge or MCP-specific quota was found.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Vendor docs state AI clients see only datasets in flows routed to that AI client as a destination. The public repository says hosted operations can be feature-flagged. The product page has a free trial; plan and account constraints may apply. Endpoint-specific plan requirements are not stated in official pricing.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Coupler.io and the workspace/account administrator; dataset exposure is configured per destination in Coupler.io.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Hosted docs distinguish read-only SQL queries from configuration changes; no hosted tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) were published. The separate local server exposes four tools and declares idempotentHint on two read tools; it is not the hosted endpoint. 2. Hosted docs say the AI is instructed to confirm before changes it was not asked to make; confirmation depends on the request and client. No server-enforced confirmation parameter or approval workflow was found. 3. Input endpoint OAuth scope is mcp; metadata advertises auth code, PKCE S256, DCR, and token auth method none. Token duration, revocation, role inheritance, admin switches, redirect approval, and allowlists: Unknown. Workspace destination routing limits datasets visible per AI tool. 4. No hosted read-only mode, toolset filter, query-free mode, or sandbox endpoint documented. Docs describe per-tool destination routing; repository lists feature-flagged hosted setup tools and account-specific URL on mcp.coupler.io. 5. Docs say the AI sees only datasets routed to it and support shaping data to hide fields and filter rows before exposure. No MCP-side PII masking or secret redaction behavior documented. 6. No endpoint-specific rate limits, quotas, result caps, or per-call costs found. General product plan caps and client consumption limits may constrain usage; docs state Custom MCP has no hard data limit. 7. Hosted parameter validation/correction is undocumented. The local code strictly validates schemas and rejects unknown parameters; its get-data query must begin SELECT. 8. Hosted MCP logging, audit trails, and telemetry specifics are undocumented. Custom plan pricing lists audit logs as a product feature; local server logs locally. Privacy policy describes general product usage collection, not MCP-specific event payloads. 9. No feedback/rating/report/survey tool appears in the hosted tool list. No MCP-specific upsell response was found. 10. Hosted server exposes list-skills/get-skill and update-dataset for context; separate skills are also described in vendor content. AI confirmation language is instruction-level, not documented enforcement. 11. Saved dataset business context persists for later use; docs say Skills and context can be reused across conversations/team members. 12. Hosted server is documented as a shared MCP infrastructure behind AI integrations and Custom MCP; the input endpoint uses a different host/auth domain than the vendor-documented host. It routes data by configured destinations. 13. get-data is the documented query tool; it runs SQL on a dataset. No arbitrary API, shell, or script tool was listed. Local source runs SQLite queries in read-only mode.

E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: A human can create and configure data flows through Coupler.io's UI, use all product integrations and account functions, and manage their subscription. The documented MCP tools provide selected data analysis and flow/configuration functions, not the full Coupler.io product interface or every integration setting. General product pricing and plan limits are documented; no complete MCP-to-UI parity list was found. F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Docs instruct the AI to confirm before making unrequested workspace changes; they say run-dataflow is only done when asked. No hosted server enforcement mechanism was documented. Docs recommend routing each flow to the intended AI destination and checking fields/rows exposed. Verbatim: “The AI only does this when you ask.” and “the AI is instructed to confirm with you before making one you didn't ask for.” Source: https://docs.coupler.io/ai/mcp.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Vendor docs state that an AI client sees only datasets from flows configured for that destination and that SQL queries cannot edit, delete, or overwrite imported rows. Blog guidance says users can hide sensitive fields and filter rows before exposure; it also cautions, “Anyone with the token and endpoint can read the data sets routed to it.” The local repository separately claims scoped, read-only, short-lived tokens; not attributed to the input hosted endpoint. Sources: https://docs.coupler.io/ai/mcp; https://blog.coupler.io/how-to-use-coupler-mcp-server/; https://github.com/coupler-io/coupler-io-mcp-server/blob/550ec75cb48bbbe0be286577b30c3a32f9bb0eea/README.md#L217-L221.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Vendor describes MCP as allowing natural-language analysis over Coupler.io data flows, server-side SQL calculations, and access to large datasets without loading all records into the AI context. Official repository says calculations are executed and verified by Coupler.io's Analytical Engine; this claim describes the product, not verified code for the input endpoint.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Destination-based visibility and read-only data queries are explicitly documented; the exact hosted enforcement code was unavailable. Confirmation is described as an AI instruction dependent on client/request, not a documented server-side guard. Field hiding and row filtering are configured in data preparation before exposure. OAuth proves endpoint authentication is required but does not establish permission inheritance, token lifetime, or audit behavior.

contradictions: Input endpoint and OAuth metadata use mcp.couplerio.dev / auth.couplerio.dev, while official vendor documentation, pricing, and repository identify the hosted MCP as mcp.coupler.io. No official source found that explains this domain difference.
The official docs tool list names 24 hosted tools, and the official repository README's hosted list additionally names list-dataflows. The exact endpoint list remains unverified.

Claude's third-party connector directory lists only get-data and get-schema, fewer than the 24 names on the official docs page and the 25 distinct names across official docs and hosted README. The listing uses connector URL https://mcp.coupler.io/mcp/.

Official hosted docs describe a broad, configurable toolset with configuration writes; the official public local server has only four read-only tools. The repository identifies it as a separate self-hosted variant, so its tools and restrictions do not establish the deployed endpoint's implementation.
observations_for_research: Dataset visibility is described as destination-specific: an AI client sees only flows configured for that client, while the built-in Coupler.io AI Agent is described as having workspace-wide dataset access.
Hosted tool availability varies by client and may be feature-flagged; the official repository calls the hosted set continuously growing.
Public OAuth metadata exposes a single scope, mcp, despite tool documentation spanning both read operations and workspace configuration changes.
